title: Does money make you happy?
idea: Happiness series pilot: Spud robs a bank because rich potatoes look happy, buys everything, and is only afraid of losing it; he flees from a siren that was never for him, his car runs dry on the coast, and the sunset gives him the smile the money didn't
format: series: Spud looks for happiness (one life question per episode, never answered out loud)

visible.why: frame 0: Spud in his fur coat and gold chain at the wheel of a gold car, rain on the glass, money bags piled behind him, his face empty
noon, a coffee cart: dirty, sad Spud reaches for a coffee; the seller holds out his palm; Spud turns out his empty pockets and shows two empty hands
behind him a rich couple in fur, pearls and velvet laugh by their white limousine with shopping bags; he stares, then wonders
a bank counter: Spud in a black balaclava points a revolver at the terrified cashier and beckons; she pushes two sacks of money over the counter to him
night street: he runs from the bank with a sack, police cars race past, he hides at the corner and laughs
the white mansion by day, a fountain, the gold car: Spud in his fur coat throws his arms wide
night, the huge marble hall: kneeling by a hole in the floor, a siren's blue and red sweeps the windows; he pushes the money sacks into the hole and shuts the tile
the front door: ten locks snap shut; Chip knocks with a gift at the side window in the rain; Spud backs away and does not open
the loneliest picture: Spud tiny at the far end of a very long table, one candle
the mansion gate at night, red and blue light on the wet drive from beyond the gate: he runs to his car with a sack
back in the car, the rain: he looks down at the dash
the fuel needle drops to empty
the gold car rolls to a stop at the roadside; a puff from the exhaust; the lamps die
he climbs the cliff with one sack, looking back: an ambulance passes below and goes; nobody was ever coming
the cliff top: Spud sits small with the sack beside him; the grey deck breaks open into a huge sunset over the sea
close: the wind takes the notes out of the open sack; he lets them go and smiles for the first time
